newsitem.title: UK: UK's Ofwat outlines rebates for under-investment.
newsitem.headline: UK's Ofwat outlines rebates for under-investment.

text.p: Britain's water industry regulator Ofwat said on Thursday that agreements with companies on rebates to customers for under-investment would mean savings of around 1.30 stg per household in 1997-98.

Ofwat head Ian Byatt said in a statement that several companies had agreed not to take up their full price increase allowances in April this year to compensate for delays in capital expenditure from previously agreed plans.
"I have suggested to the companies (underinvesting) that this was one of the factors they should consider in deciding their charges from next April," Byatt said.
Hyder, Northumbrian which is now owned by France's Lyonnaise des Eaux, Severn Trent, Southern and Yorkshire Water have all agreed not to put up prices by the maximum allowed next year.
Some companies have planned rebates to customers but Thames Water argued that any savings should be put into discretionary expenditure.
